overview: Two successive structures formed in the ovary after ovulation, one hormonally active and the other its inactive scar-like remnant.
genZNote: Corpus luteum: actively working, pumping out progesterone. Corpus albicans: retired, just scar tissue left behind.

aspects.label: Function
aspects.valueA: An active, hormone-secreting structure producing progesterone (and some estrogen).
aspects.valueB: A non-functional, fibrous scar tissue — has no hormonal activity.

aspects.label: Formed From
aspects.valueB: The degenerated corpus luteum, if pregnancy does not occur.

aspects.label: Fate If Pregnancy Occurs
aspects.valueA: Maintained and enlarged by hCG, continuing to support early pregnancy.
aspects.valueB: Only forms if pregnancy does NOT occur — the corpus luteum degenerates into it.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: If fertilisation occurs, hCG from the developing embryo rescues the corpus luteum from degenerating into a corpus albicans.
overlay.memoryTrick: Luteum = 'yellow body', active. Albicans = 'white body', dead scar tissue.
overlay.commonMisconception: The corpus albicans does not secrete any hormones — once formed, it is functionally inert scar tissue.
